system_overview: A model-checking configuration module for the practical MultiPaxos specification. It extends the main protocol specification and defines type-checking invariants and a linearizability safety constraint for verification. The linearizability check ensures that the sequence of client-observed request and acknowledgement events is consistent with some valid sequential execution order that respects real-time ordering.
actors_and_components: Inherits all actors from the main MultiPaxos specification: server replicas, implicit clients, and the asynchronous network. This module adds symmetry reduction definitions and the linearizability checking logic.
state_variables: Inherits all state variables from the MultiPaxos specification: network messages, per-replica node state, pending commands, and observed client events.
actions: Inherited from the MultiPaxos specification without modification.
safety_properties: Two safety properties are checked. (1) Type correctness: all messages conform to the message type, all node states are well-typed, the pending sequence length and uniqueness constraints hold, and observed events are valid client events with consistent request/acknowledgement counts. (2) Linearizability: upon termination, there must exist a total order on all commands such that the order is a valid sequential execution (each read returns the value of the most recent preceding write) and the order respects the real-time constraint (if one command's acknowledgement precedes another command's request in the observed sequence, then the first command must precede the second in the linear order).
liveness_properties: Deadlock checking is enabled, serving as a semi-liveness check ensuring the system makes progress until all commands are processed.
model_bounds: The default configuration uses 3 server replicas, 2 write commands, 1 read command, and a maximum ballot of 2. Symmetry reduction is applied over permutations of replicas, writes, and reads (only when the set has more than one element). A smaller configuration variant uses 1 write command for faster checking.
additional_assumptions: The linearizability constraint is defined in terms of client-observed events and is checked only upon termination (when all commands have been requested and acknowledged). The linear order is existentially quantified as a sequence containing all commands. Helper operators extract the position of each command's request and acknowledgement in the observed sequence, determine the result (old value) returned by each command, and identify the last write before any given position in the linear order.
